howItWorks:
HOW THE CLIMB TAG CURRENTLY WORKS (verified end-to-end against source):

A `.climbName` overlay is a styled "lower-third" `OverlayItem` (StudioProject.swift:175-261). Crucially, `OverlayItem` has NO clip reference — it has only a flat output-time window (`startSec`/`endSec`, lines 186-187) plus position/style/opacityKeyframes. The doc comment (line 173) is explicit: an overlay is "Visible while startSec ≤ playhead ≤ endSec".

ADD PATH: The "Climb" action button (StudioEditorView.swift:270) is a stateless fire-every-tap button — `barButton("Climb", "signpost.right", enabled: vm.hasClimbInfo) { vm.addClimbNameOverlay() }`. It is enabled whenever `hasClimbInfo` (VM:419: `resolvedClimbUUID != nil || suggestedClimbCaption != nil`) and shows no ✓/selected state (unlike Music/HR at lines 264/272). `addClimbNameOverlay()` (VM:426-440) builds the caption (from the resolved Kilter climb, or the freeform `suggestedClimbCaption`), then UNCONDITIONALLY constructs a fresh `OverlayItem(kind: .climbName, ... startSec: 0, endSec: max(3, totalDuration), position: (0.5, 0.85))` and appends it via `editOverlaysOnly { StudioProjectEditor.addOverlay($0, overlay) }`. `addOverlay` is a pure append (StudioProjectEditor.swift:199-201: `s.overlays.append(overlay)`) with no de-dup/lookup. So (a) the window is hardcoded to the WHOLE project (0…totalDuration), tied to no clip, and (b) there is no existence check — N taps create N overlays.

ATTEMPT LINE: `setSelectedClimbShowsAttempt` (VM:497-509) appends "Attempt N" using `effectiveAttemptNumber` = `selectedClipAttemptNumber ?? suggestedAttemptNumber` (VM:477), where `selectedClipAttemptNumber` reads the SELECTED clip's `SessionMedia.assignedSetIndex+1` (VM:467-472). On clip selection, `select(_:)` (VM:303-308) calls `refreshAttemptLineForSelection()`, which re-derives the attempt line — but only on `selectedOverlay` (whichever overlay `selectedOverlayID` points at), which is independent of the selected clip.

RENDER (two divergent paths): The WYSIWYG editor canvas (StudioOverlayCanvas.swift:54) renders `ForEach(overlays)` with NO time/playhead gate — the struct has no `currentTime` member at all (lines 15-33), and the view passes `vm.overlays` unfiltered (StudioEditorView.swift:165). The EXPORT path (StudioOverlays.applyVisibility, :788-826) DOES gate each layer's opacity to `[startSec,endSec]`. But because every climb tag's window is 0…totalDuration, export still burns all of them in for the whole reel.

WHY BUG #1 (overlays span the whole project, not the clip): `addClimbNameOverlay()` hardcodes `startSec:0, endSec:max(3,totalDuration)` (VM:435-437) and never reads the selected clip's output slot — even though `placedClips` (VM:173-176 → StudioGeometry.timeline) already exposes each clip's `startSec`/`durationSec`/`endSec` (StudioGeometry.swift:51-80), correctly accounting for order/trim/speed/transitions. So in "Edit all clips" every tag's window is the entire timeline. In the editor they all show because the canvas isn't time-gated; in export they all burn in because the window is the whole reel.

WHY BUG #2 (re-adds a new box on each touch): the add path is not idempotent (no `first(where: kind == .climbName)` lookup anywhere — grep-confirmed), and the button has no toggled/selected state, so each tap appends another lower-third. Because each tag also spans the whole project and the canvas shows everything, the duplicates all appear at once. The differing "Attempt 1/2/blank" lines in the screenshot are explained by the user tapping Climb while different clips were selected and toggling Attempt# per selection — the trio is a direct product of #1 + #2.
rootCauses: No clip linkage on OverlayItem (StudioProject.swift:175-261): the model carries only a flat [startSec,endSec] window and no clipID/sessionMediaID, so "this tag belongs to clip X" is inexpressible — the root that forces both bugs and breaks on trim/reorder/split.

addClimbNameOverlay() hardcodes startSec:0, endSec:max(3,totalDuration) (StudioEditorViewModel.swift:435-437), ignoring the selected clip's output slot (which placedClips/StudioGeometry.timeline already provides).

addClimbNameOverlay() has no idempotency/existence guard (StudioEditorViewModel.swift:426-440) and StudioProjectEditor.addOverlay is a pure append (StudioProjectEditor.swift:199-201); the Climb button (StudioEditorView.swift:270) is a stateless fire-every-tap action with no toggled/✓ state.

The WYSIWYG canvas (StudioOverlayCanvas.swift:15-33, 54) has no currentTime member and renders ForEach(overlays) with no [startSec,endSec] gate, so preview != export and any window fix is invisible in the editor until the canvas is time-gated.
scopedSnapshot scopes only clips, never overlays (StudioEditorViewModel.swift:145-150), and export() uses it (line 965) — so even a scoped/per-clip export still carries (and burns in) every overlay.

Clip selection and overlay selection are decoupled: select(_:) sets selectedClipID and calls refreshAttemptLineForSelection() but never repoints selectedOverlayID (StudioEditorViewModel.swift:303-308, 516-522), so the dynamic attempt# mutates the last-selected overlay, not the newly-selected clip's tag.

bugs.title: BUG #1 (user-reported): Climb tag spans the whole project instead of the selected clip — all tags render simultaneously in editor AND export
bugs.rootCause: StudioEditorViewModel.swift:435-437 — addClimbNameOverlay() hardcodes `OverlayItem(kind: .climbName, ..., startSec: 0, endSec: max(3, totalDuration), position: (0.5, 0.85))`, with no tie to the selected clip's output slot. OverlayItem has no clip field (StudioProject.swift:175-261). In "Edit all clips" totalDuration spans all attempt clips (VM:161-164), so every climb tag's window is the entire timeline. Export gates by window (StudioOverlays.applyVisibility:788-826) but 0…total = on for the whole reel; the canvas isn't gated at all (StudioOverlayCanvas.swift:54), so they all show in the editor too. Verified: placedClips/StudioGeometry.timeline (VM:173-176, StudioGeometry.swift:51-80) already exposes the correct per-clip [startSec,endSec].
bugs.fix: Anchor the overlay to the selected clip's placed slot on creation: `guard let clip = selectedClip, let slot = placedClips.first(where: { $0.clip.id == clip.id }) else { /* whole-project fallback */ }` then create with `startSec: slot.startSec, endSec: slot.endSec`. Keep a whole-project fallback when no clip is selected (the Climb button is tappable with selectedClip == nil in "Edit all clips"). Because export already time-gates via applyVisibility, NO export-side change is needed for confinement once the window is correct. Recompute the window on trim/split/reorder (it would otherwise go stale) — see fix plan.

bugs.title: BUG #2 (user-reported): "Climb" button re-adds a new overlay on every tap (not idempotent) — the 3 stacked duplicates
bugs.rootCause: StudioEditorViewModel.swift:426-440 — addClimbNameOverlay() unconditionally builds and appends a fresh OverlayItem; StudioProjectEditor.addOverlay (StudioProjectEditor.swift:199-201) is a pure `s.overlays.append(overlay)` with no de-dup. No `first(where: kind == .climbName)`/add-or-update lookup exists anywhere (grep-confirmed). The button (StudioEditorView.swift:270) is a stateless action with no toggled/✓ state (contrast Music ✓ / HR ✓ at :264/:272). Each tap stacks another lower-third; combined with #1 they all show at once.
bugs.fix: Make the add idempotent and scoped to the selected clip: if a `.climbName` overlay already exists for the selected clip's slot, just set `selectedOverlayID = existing.id` and return; otherwise add. Until a clipID field exists, key on the selected clip's resolved [startSec,endSec] window — NOT a bare `first(where: kind == .climbName)`, which would wrongly collapse legitimately-distinct per-clip tags once #1 lands. Reflect state on the button ("Climb ✓") to match Music/HR. Land together with #1 (the dedup key depends on #1's per-clip scoping).

bugs.title: OverlayItem cannot reference a clip — "belongs to clip X" is inexpressible and a snapshotted window desyncs on trim/split/reorder/speed/transition changes
bugs.rootCause: StudioProject.swift:175-261 — OverlayItem has id/kindRaw/content/startSec/endSec/position/scale/style/opacityKeyframes but NO clipID/sessionMediaID. Clip→output mapping is dynamic (StudioGeometry.timeline:63-80 derives each slot from cumulative output durations minus transition overlaps); moveClip/trimClip/splitClip recompute (StudioProjectEditor.swift:64-77+) and nothing rebinds overlays. So #1's window-only fix is correct on creation but goes stale after a structural edit (reorder after tagging mis-places the tag).
bugs.fix: Add an additive-optional `var clipID: UUID? = nil` (or `boundClipID`) to OverlayItem — migration-safe per the file's stated optional-field convention (highlightHex/font fields at :193-209 prove the pattern). Set it in addClimbNameOverlay() to selectedClip?.id. RESOLVE the export/preview window from clipID → the clip's current placed slot at render time (mirroring the composer's PlacedClipHR pattern that already maps clip→slot, StudioOverlays.swift:38,63-69), rather than baking a static window — this keeps the tag correct across reorder/trim. The export side (applyVisibility) reads stored startSec/endSec, so either re-derive into those fields before makeAnimationTool or pass a per-clip window map alongside (sibling to clipHR).

bugs.title: WYSIWYG canvas renders ALL overlays regardless of playhead — preview != export even after the window fix
bugs.rootCause: StudioOverlayCanvas.swift:54 iterates `ForEach(overlays)` with no time predicate; the struct (lines 15-33) has no currentTime/playhead member; StudioEditorView.swift:165 passes vm.overlays and no playhead. Export gates per window (StudioOverlays.swift:788-826). So even after #1 the editor preview would still show every climb tag (and #2's duplicates) at all playhead positions. vm.currentTime already exists (StudioEditorViewModel.swift:64) and drives the playhead readout.
bugs.fix: Thread `currentTime: vm.currentTime` into StudioOverlayCanvas and gate the ForEach to overlays whose `[startSec,endSec]` contains the playhead — `ForEach(overlays.filter { $0.id == selectedID || (currentTime >= $0.startSec - eps && currentTime <= $0.endSec + eps) })` — but ALWAYS render the selected overlay (so a just-added/off-segment tag stays draggable/editable). Use a small epsilon and clamp at clip boundaries (StudioGeometry pulls clips earlier by transition overlap, so adjacent slots can touch). Apply the same gate to .text/.sticker chips (export already does). Land with #1.
bugs.fixNote: Mandatory companion to #1 — the window fix is invisible in the editor without it.

bugs.title: Dynamic attempt# mutates the LAST-SELECTED overlay, not the overlay belonging to the newly-selected clip
bugs.rootCause: StudioEditorViewModel.swift:303-308 — select(_:) sets selectedClipID and calls refreshAttemptLineForSelection() but never repoints selectedOverlayID. refreshAttemptLineForSelection (:516-522) and setSelectedClimbShowsAttempt (:497-509) both act on selectedOverlay (= overlays.first { $0.id == selectedOverlayID }, :156), which is driven solely by selectedOverlayID. Clip-tap (StudioTimelineView.swift:112 select(p.clip.id)) and overlay-tap (selectOverlay) are independent. So switching clip A→B re-derives B's effectiveAttemptNumber but writes it onto whatever overlay was last selected (typically A's / the last-added tag); B's own tag is left stale. Depends on #3's clip link to fix properly.
bugs.fix: In select(_:), after #1/#3 land, repoint selectedOverlayID to the .climbName overlay owned by the newly-selected clip (its clipID), or to nil if that clip has no climb tag (so the Attempt#/setter toggles don't act on an unrelated tag). Then refreshAttemptLineForSelection mutates the right overlay. Once both base caption and attempt number derive from the overlay's owning clip, the multi-clip attempt# becomes correct.

bugs.title: Climb-tag Attempt#/Setter toggle state lives in transient in-memory Sets — desyncs from the persisted caption across reopen and undo/redo
bugs.rootCause: StudioEditorViewModel.swift:414 (climbSetterEnabled) and :460 (climbAttemptEnabled) are plain `private var Set<UUID>`, never persisted and never reconstructed from captions; init (:73-81) seeds them empty. selectedClimbShowsAttempt (:488-491) / selectedClimbShowsSetter (:443-446) read ONLY the Sets. StudioProjectSnapshot doesn't include them, and undoEdit/redoEdit (:299-300) restore the caption but not the Sets. So after reopen a caption ending in "Attempt 2" reads toggle-OFF and the dynamic refresh silently stops; after undo, caption and toggle disagree. (Note: re-toggling does NOT double the line — climbTagBase regex strips the prior \nAttempt N first.)
bugs.fix: Stop using transient Sets for source-of-truth. Best: persist explicit fields on OverlayItem (showsAttempt: Bool, attempt: Int?, showsSetter: Bool) and compose the rendered string from base + flags (also fixes the regex over-match below). Minimal: derive selectedClimbShowsAttempt from the caption via `content.range(of: #"\nAttempt \d+$"#, options: .regularExpression) != nil` (no persistence needed, fixes undo/reopen for attempt). Setter has no string marker — persist a flag or re-derive by comparing to the with/without-setter caption. Seed/reconcile on load and on undo/redo.

bugs.title: climbTagBase strip regex destroys a user-typed trailing "Attempt N" line in the caption (silent caption corruption)
bugs.rootCause: StudioEditorViewModel.swift:528-533 — climbTagBase strips ANY trailing `\nAttempt \d+$`. It runs from setSelectedClimbShowsAttempt (:500) AND refreshAttemptLineForSelection (:519, called from select() on EVERY clip change). The caption is freely editable via the pencil (StudioEditorView.swift:307-310 → editOverlayText). Verified by executing the function: climbTagBase("My project\nAttempt 3") => "My project". So merely changing the selected clip (not just toggling) can silently delete a user's line.
bugs.fix: Don't infer the appended line from a generic regex over user content. Track the last-appended attempt value per overlay (e.g. the attempt: Int? field from the bug above) and only strip the trailing line when its N equals the value WE appended; or store base + showsAttempt/attempt as explicit fields and compose, so user text and the system line never share an encoding. This single structural change resolves this and the toggle-state desync together.

bugs.title: "Show setter" toggle is shown but is a dead no-op for freeform climbs (no KilterLogEntry)
bugs.rootCause: StudioEditorView.swift:319-323 renders the "Show setter" Toggle for EVERY .climbName overlay (gated only on ov.kind == .climbName). setSelectedClimbShowsSetter (StudioEditorViewModel.swift:450-455) early-returns unless resolvedClimbUUID != nil. resolvedClimbUUID (:536-547) reads SessionMedia.assignedClimbUUID, which is only ever written by Kilter flows (KilterClimbPanel.swift:196, KilterSessionDetailView.swift:540, KilterBoardController.swift:771 — never in the freeform path). So for a freeform climb it's nil, the guard returns, and the Toggle springs back OFF. Confusing dead control.
bugs.fix: Add `var canShowClimbSetter: Bool { selectedOverlay?.kind == .climbName && resolvedClimbUUID != nil }` and wrap the Toggle in `if vm.canShowClimbSetter`, mirroring the existing canShowClimbAttempt gating (StudioEditorView.swift:326). Optionally also require a non-empty setter so it hides for Kilter climbs that have none.

bugs.title: "Show setter" toggle silently discards the user's manual caption edits (Kilter clips only)
bugs.rootCause: StudioEditorViewModel.swift:450-455 — setSelectedClimbShowsSetter regenerates the caption wholesale via `climbCaption(uuid:includeSetter:)` and editOverlayText, never reading ov.content (its own doc comment admits "Resets any manual text edit"). Contrast the Attempt# path (:497-509) which preserves the base via climbTagBase. Scope caveat: this only bites Kilter clips, since the setter path is a no-op for freeform (resolvedClimbUUID == nil — see prior bug).
bugs.fix: Make the setter toggle additive — compute only the " · by {setter}" suffix and append/strip it on the existing detail line of ov.content rather than regenerating. Hiding the toggle for freeform (canShowClimbSetter gate) removes most exposure. Naturally subsumed once captions become base + explicit flags.

bugs.title: Deleting a clip leaves its climb-name (and other) overlays orphaned and still rendering
bugs.rootCause: StudioProjectEditor.removeClip (StudioProjectEditor.swift:62-68) filters s.clips and the trailing transition only — never touches s.overlays. deleteSelected (StudioEditorViewModel.swift:310-314) clears selectedClipID, also not touching overlays. Because a climb tag is whole-timeline [0,total] with no clip linkage today, deleting its clip leaves the tag floating over the remaining clips; once clipID exists (#3) this becomes a concrete dangling reference.
bugs.fix: After clipID lands (#3): in removeClip, `s.overlays.removeAll { $0.clipID == id }`. Lighter alternative that avoids the schema dependency for the climb case: after removeClip recomputes the timeline, garbage-collect or re-clamp any overlay whose [startSec,endSec] now falls entirely outside the new totalDuration. removeClip is only called from deleteSelected, so scoping the prune there is safe.

bugs.title: Preview chip ignores opacityKeyframes and floors opacity at 0.15 — keyframed/low-opacity climb tags look different in export
bugs.rootCause: StudioOverlayCanvas.swift styledText uses a single static `.opacity(max(0.15, overlay.opacity))` and never samples overlay.opacityKeyframes; export bakes the keyframes and clamps with a 0 floor (StudioOverlays.swift:797-815). addOverlayKeyframeAtPlayhead applies to any selected overlay incl. climbName (StudioEditorViewModel.swift:931-936). So a faded/keyframed climb tag previews flat at 0.15 but exports animated to full transparency.
bugs.fix: Coupled to the canvas-time fix: once currentTime is threaded in (#4), sample opacity from opacityKeyframes at the playhead and drop the 0.15 floor to match export's 0 floor (or, if 0.15 is an intentional editor-legibility minimum, apply the same floor in applyVisibility so both agree). Do it in the same change as the canvas time-gate.

bugs.title: Empty resolved caption produces an invisible, selectable climb chip on the canvas (narrow data edge)
bugs.rootCause: KilterClimbCaption.caption can return an empty detailLine when name is empty; export filters empty-content overlays (StudioOverlays.swift:41 `!$0.content.isEmpty`) but the canvas does NOT (StudioOverlayCanvas.swift:62-67 renders TextOverlayChip regardless), yielding a near-zero-size selectable chip. Reachability is a narrow data edge (a Kilter entry with empty name+grade+angle and no setter).
bugs.fix: Guard addClimbNameOverlay() to no-op (or use a "Climb" placeholder) when the resolved caption is empty after trimming, and filter empty-content chips out of the canvas ForEach to match the export filter.

fixPlan: STEP 1 (model — enables everything): Add an additive-optional `var clipID: UUID? = nil` to OverlayItem (StudioProject.swift, follow the highlightHex/font optional-field migration pattern at :193-209). Migration-safe; old projects decode nil. This is the one schema change that makes the climb tag a true per-clip property and unblocks idempotency, clip-scoped windows, correct multi-clip attempt#, and orphan cleanup. Pure time-window scoping alone (no clipID) fixes the reported render bug on CREATION but cannot survive trim/reorder/split and cannot key idempotency robustly — so add the field.

STEP 2 (BUG #1 — confine to clip): In addClimbNameOverlay() (StudioEditorViewModel.swift:435-437) set clipID = selectedClip?.id and the window from the selected clip's placed slot — `placedClips.first(where: { $0.clip.id == selectedClip?.id })` → startSec/endSec — with a whole-project fallback when no clip is selected. Resolve the export window from clipID → current placed slot AT RENDER TIME (mirror the composer's PlacedClipHR clip→slot map, StudioOverlays.swift:38/63-69) so reorder/trim stay correct rather than baking a static window. Export already time-gates via applyVisibility, so no applyVisibility change is needed beyond feeding it the resolved window.

STEP 3 (BUG #2 — idempotent add-or-select): In addClimbNameOverlay(), first look up `overlays.first { $0.kind == .climbName && $0.clipID == selectedClip?.id }`; if found, set selectedOverlayID = existing.id and return (optionally re-seed its base caption); else add. Reflect state on the button ("Climb ✓", StudioEditorView.swift:270) like Music/HR. Land STEPS 2+3 together — the dedup key depends on per-clip scoping.

STEP 4 (canvas time-gate — makes #1 visible in the editor): Add `currentTime: vm.currentTime` to StudioOverlayCanvas (StudioEditorView.swift:165) and a stored currentTime member; in the ForEach (StudioOverlayCanvas.swift:54) render an overlay only when `selected || startSec-eps <= currentTime <= endSec+eps`, always keeping the selected overlay visible so it stays draggable off-segment. Apply to .text/.sticker too. Land with STEPS 2/3 — mandatory companion, not optional.

STEP 5 (multi-clip attempt# correctness): In select(_:) (StudioEditorViewModel.swift:303-308) repoint selectedOverlayID to the .climbName overlay owned by the newly-selected clip (by clipID), or nil if none, BEFORE/with refreshAttemptLineForSelection(). Then the dynamic Attempt N is re-derived onto the correct per-clip tag, and the resolvedClimbUUID/attempt mix-up dissolves because both base caption and attempt derive from the overlay's owning clip.

STEP 6 (caption/toggle robustness): Replace the transient climbAttemptEnabled/climbSetterEnabled Sets with explicit persisted OverlayItem fields (showsAttempt: Bool, attempt: Int?, showsSetter: Bool) and compose the rendered string from base + flags. This fixes (a) toggle state desync on reopen/undo (read state from the model, not memory), (b) the climbTagBase regex destroying user-typed "Attempt N" lines (system line no longer shares an encoding with user text), and (c) the setter toggle discarding manual edits (make it additive). Reconcile on load and on undo/redo.

STEP 7 (lifecycle + polish, low risk, independent): (a) In removeClip, `s.overlays.removeAll { $0.clipID == id }` (or re-clamp overlays whose window now falls outside totalDuration). (b) Gate the "Show setter" toggle behind `canShowClimbSetter` (resolvedClimbUUID != nil) so it's hidden for freeform. (c) When the backing SessionMedia changes via KilterClimbPanel, notify the studio VM to re-derive captions/attempt. (d) Honor opacityKeyframes + drop the 0.15 floor in the canvas (do with STEP 4). (e) No-op/placeholder for empty captions and filter empty chips from the canvas. (f) Add accessibility label/value/.isSelected + identifier to TextOverlayChip.
modelChangeNeeded: A model field on OverlayItem IS recommended (not strictly required for the reported bug today, but required to do it right). Add an additive-optional `var clipID: UUID? = nil` to OverlayItem (StudioProject.swift:175-261), following the existing migration-safe optional-field convention (highlightHex/fontRaw/boldRaw/italicRaw at lines 193-209 prove old projects decode nil). WHY: OverlayItem currently has only a flat [startSec,endSec] window and no clip reference, so \"this tag belongs to clip X\" is inexpressible. Pure time-window scoping (no field) DOES fix both user-reported bugs at creation time — set startSec/endSec from the selected clip's placed slot and key idempotency on that window — and is the minimal change. BUT a snapshotted window goes stale on trim/split/reorder/speed/transition edits (StudioGeometry.timeline recomputes slots and nothing rebinds overlays), and a window-only idempotency key is brittle. clipID lets you (1) re-derive the export/preview window from the clip's CURRENT placed slot at render time (mirroring the composer's PlacedClipHR clip→slot pattern) so it never desyncs, (2) key idempotency reliably (\"a .climbName for this clip already exists\"), (3) repoint selection per clip for correct multi-clip attempt#, and (4) garbage-collect orphans on clip delete. Optionally also add explicit per-tag fields (showsAttempt/attempt/showsSetter) to replace the transient toggle-state Sets and the fragile caption-regex (STEP 6). All additive-optional → Codable-migration-safe.
